newsitem.title: USA: Imo backs away from selling unit, may sue.
newsitem.headline: Imo backs away from selling unit, may sue.

text.p: Imo Industries Inc said Monday it was withdrawing the potential sale of its subsidiary, Roltra-Morse, alleging that the unsuccessful bidder, Keikert AG, has threatened to revoke certain license agreements if it were sold to competitors.

The move prompted Imo to restate its third quarter results to reclassify Roltra as a continuing operation, leading to an operating loss of $0.73 per share instead of an operating profit of $0.14 per share from the prior year.
The restated results for the period amounted to a net loss of $1.16 per share versus a net loss of $0.28 per share in the same period in the prior year.

The company said the restated results place it in technical default of certain financial covenents of its revolving credit agreements. It said it is negotiating with banks that are part of the credit agreement to secure a waiver, which it expects to receive.
Imo Industries, a manufacturer of pumps, fluid sensors, power transmission products, remote control systems and automotive components, said it intends to sue the unsuccessful bidder, Kiekert AG.
Imo contends Kiekert has acted to block the sale of the Roltra-Morse unit, which manufactures components for the automobile industry.
"Kiekert's tactics have jeopardized our ability to receive fair value for Roltra, and we intend to seek full restitution," Imo Chairman and Chief Executive Donald Farrar said in a statement.
The company said it expects fourth quarter results will be hurt by the Roltra-Morse situation and a restructuring of the business. It said it expects an overall loss in the fourth quarter.
In October, Imo had reported net income of $801,000, or $0.05 per share for the third quarter.
